word: I didn't even know what a pancreas was.
meaning: 我甚至不知道胰腺是什麼。
example: He had no idea what a pancreas was before receiving this diagnosis.
hint:
中文解釋：帶點苦澀幽默的自我嘲諷——面對一個連器官名稱都不熟悉的癌症，突顯了震驚與無力感。
1) even (adv.): 甚至；syn: so much as; ant: at least
2) pancreas (n.): 胰腺（消化系統器官）；syn: digestive gland; ant: (n/a)
pronunciation: Self-deprecating: I did-n't EVEN know | what a PAN-cre-as WAS. (slight irony)

word: The doctors told me this was almost certainly a type of cancer that is incurable, and that I should expect to live no longer than three to six months.
meaning: 醫生告訴我，這幾乎可以確定是一種無法治癒的癌症，我的預期壽命不超過三到六個月。
example: His doctors said it was likely incurable cancer and that he had only three to six months to live.
hint:
中文解釋：宣判性的死亡診斷——三到六個月，讓一切顯得如此真實和緊迫。
1) incurable (adj.): 無法治癒的；syn: untreatable; ant: curable
2) expect to live (phr.): 預期能活多長；syn: life expectancy; ant: (n/a)
pronunciation: Grave: al-MOST CER-tain-ly | a type of can-cer that is in-CUR-a-ble | LIVE no LON-ger than THREE to SIX MONTHS.

word: My doctor advised me to go home and get my affairs in order, which is doctors' code for 'Prepare to die.'
meaning: 我的醫生建議我回家，把一切事務安排好，這是醫生暗語，意思是「準備死亡」。
example: His doctor's suggestion to 'get his affairs in order' was a polite way of saying he should prepare to die.
hint:
中文解釋：「get affairs in order」是醫學委婉語，Jobs 直接點破其真實含義，展現他一貫的直率。
1) get affairs in order (phr.): 安排好一切事務；syn: prepare for death; ant: plan for the future
2) code for (phr.): 是…的暗語；syn: means; ant: (n/a)
pronunciation: Pointed: get my AF-fairs in OR-der | DOC-tors' CODE | for PRE-pare to DIE.

word: It means to try and tell your kids everything you thought you'd have the next ten years to tell them in just a few months.
meaning: 它的意思是，試著在幾個月之內，把你以為還有十年可以告訴孩子的一切都說完。
example: It means compressing a lifetime of important conversations with your children into just a few months.
hint:
中文解釋：將「prepare to die」的殘酷現實具體化——把十年的父母之愛壓縮到幾個月。
1) thought you'd have (phr.): 以為自己還有（時間）；syn: assumed you had; ant: knew you had only
2) ten years (n.): 十年；syn: a decade; ant: a few months
pronunciation: Painful: tell your KIDS eve-ry-thing | thought you'd have the NEXT TEN YEARS | in JUST a FEW MONTHS.

word: It means to make sure everything is buttoned up so that it will be as easy as possible for your family.
meaning: 它的意思是，確保一切都處理妥當，讓你的家人盡可能地輕鬆面對接下來的事。
example: It means arranging all your affairs so that your family will not face unnecessary difficulty after you are gone.
hint:
中文解釋：「buttoned up」是口語，意指「一切都整理好、無遺漏」，這句話道盡了死亡前的責任感。
1) buttoned up (phr.): 一切妥善處理、密封好；syn: sorted out; ant: left undone
2) as easy as possible (phr.): 盡可能容易；syn: smoothly; ant: as difficult as possible
pronunciation: Careful: eve-ry-thing is BUT-toned UP | as EAS-y as POS-si-ble | for your FAM-i-ly.

word: It means to say your goodbyes.
meaning: 它的意思是，跟你愛的人道別。
example: It means finding the time and words to say farewell to the people you love.
hint:
中文解釋：三個詞承載了最沉重的情感——說再見，是人類最難完成的事之一。
1) say goodbye (phr.): 道別；syn: bid farewell; ant: greet
2) your (pron.): 你的（暗示是最親近的人）；syn: loved ones'; ant: (n/a)
pronunciation: Quiet: It means | to say your GOOD-byes. (very slow, somber)

word: I lived with that diagnosis all day.
meaning: 我帶著那個診斷結果度過了整整一天。
example: He spent the entire day carrying the weight of knowing he might be dying.
hint:
中文解釋：「lived with」有「帶著這個現實生活」的意涵，傳達了那天的沉重與無助。
1) lived with (phr.): 帶著…生活、承受著；syn: carried; ant: ignored
2) all day (phr.): 整整一天；syn: the entire day; ant: briefly
pronunciation: Heavy: I LIVED with that di-AG-no-sis | ALL DAY. (slow, weighted)

word: Later that evening I had a biopsy, where they stuck an endoscope down my throat, through my stomach, and into my intestines, put a needle into my pancreas, and got a few cells from the tumor.
meaning: 當天傍晚，我做了一次切片手術——他們把內視鏡伸進我的喉嚨，穿過胃部，進入腸道，再把一根針刺入我的胰腺，取出腫瘤的幾個細胞。
example: That evening, doctors performed a biopsy, inserting a scope through his body to collect cells from the tumor.
hint:
中文解釋：詳細的醫療程序描述，讓聽眾感受到過程的侵入性與不適，也帶出後面的轉機。
1) biopsy (n.): 切片手術；syn: tissue sample; ant: (n/a)
2) endoscope (n.): 內視鏡；syn: medical camera; ant: (n/a)
pronunciation: Clinical detail: bi-OP-sy | en-do-SCOPE down my THROAT | through my STOM-ach | in-to my in-TES-tines | a NEE-dle | a FEW CELLS.
